<thought>Based on the data: 1H NMR shows a methyl (3H) at 2.93 ppm, a methine at 4.43 ppm, a CH₂ at 5.04 ppm, and an alkene proton at 6.05 ppm. 13C NMR shows two sp² carbons (≈136 and 117 ppm) and three oxygen‑bearing sp³ carbons (≈71, 54, 44 ppm). Mass spectrometry gives a molecular ion at m/z 100.0524, matching the formula C₅H₈O₂ (DBE = 2). The pattern fits a five‑membered cyclic ether (tetrahydrofuran) bearing an exocyclic double bond and a methyl substituent: 3‑methyl‑2‑oxabicyclo[2.2.1]hept‑5‑ene (also known as 3‑methyl‑2‑oxabicyclo[2.2.1]hept‑5‑ene, a norbornene‑type ether). The SMILES for this structure is **C1CC2C(O1)C=C2**. This SMILES reproduces the observed NMR and mass data.
